clue.text: Artist receives tip from Impressionist in foreign city

indicators.note: the painter's name takes another letter inside it, as if receiving it

parts.note: Edvard Munch, the Norwegian painter of The Scream

indicators.note: the tip of a word is its first letter, here of Impressionist

explanation.surface: A painter is handed advice by an Impressionist while abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tip' looks like advice, but it is just the first letter of Impressionist.
explanation.definitionFit: Munich is the Bavarian capital, so a city foreign to the British setter.

clue.text: Drain source of pus above ear

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece sits above the other, so it comes first
the source of a word is where it starts, its first letter

parts.note: lughole is British slang for the ear

explanation.surface: A grisly medical note: pus is draining from above the ear.
explanation.walkthrough: LUGHOLE is informal British for an ear; 'above' works because this is a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A plughole is the outlet in a sink or bath where water goes down, a drain.

clue.text: Badly ruing November deal when going after money — it gives offence

definitions.text: when going after money — it gives offence

indicators.note: something done badly is botched, so these letters are muddled into a new order

parts.note: N is November in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone regrets a bad deal struck over money that caused offence.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a little phrase: put the answer after 'money' and you get the name of a crime. 'Badly' is the scrambling signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Money laundering, disguising the source of dirty cash, is a criminal offence, so the word placed after money names one.

clue.text: Section of field protected by assorted canes

indicators.note: one piece is guarded by being surrounded by the other
assorted things are mixed up, so the letters of canes are jumbled

parts.note: a field is an area, as in an area of study

explanation.surface: Part of a field fenced off with a mix of canes, as in a garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Section' looks like part of the field, but it is the definition, a medical one.
explanation.definitionFit: A Caesarean section is the surgical delivery of a baby, so the word on its own can stand for that operation.

clue.text: Film lectures

definitions.meaning: as a verb, talks at length or nags someone

explanation.surface: A short note about a film of lectures.
explanation.definitionFit: Spielberg's shark movie has this title, and to jaw is slang for talking on and on, a lecture.

clue.text: Criticise current politician hugging occasionally

parts.note: I is the symbol for electric current
an MP is a Member of Parliament

indicators.note: taking letters only now and then, every other one of hugging

explanation.surface: A sitting politician is attacked for hugging people now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: 'occasionally' takes the even letters of hugging: U, G, N.
explanation.definitionFit: To impugn someone's motives or honesty is to call them into question, to attack them in words.

clue.text: Old soldier hears row erupting

indicators.note: an eruption throws things about, so these letters are scattered

explanation.surface: A veteran hears an argument break out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'erupting' rearranges HEARS ROW.
explanation.definitionFit: An old warhorse is a veteran of many battles or campaigns, a figurative term for a seasoned soldier.

clue.text: Relative, having foremost charges dropped, remains free

indicators.note: the letter is let fall out of the relative's word

parts.note: an uncle is a family relative

indicators.note: the foremost letter of charges is its first

parts.note: ash is what remains after burning

explanation.surface: A relative has the main charges against them dropped and walks free.
explanation.walkthrough: 'charges' and 'dropped' suggest a court case; only the first letter of charges is dropped from the relative.
explanation.definitionFit: To unleash is to let loose or set free, as a dog from its lead.

clue.text: Spit of land perhaps man's right to sacrifice for hotel

indicators.note: the first letter is given up in exchange for another, as a chess player sacrifices a piece

parts.note: in chess the pieces are called men, and a rook is one
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A man is right to give something up for the sake of a hotel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'man' is a chess piece, ROOK; 'sacrifice' keeps the chess picture as R is swapped for H.
explanation.definitionFit: A hook is a curved spit or headland, as in Sandy Hook; 'perhaps' marks it as one sense among several.

clue.text: Pallid condition of adolescent originally — adult I mean, on reflection

indicators.note: the original, starting letter of adolescent
a reflection in a mirror is reversed, so these pieces read backwards

parts.note: A is the film classification for adult

explanation.surface: A teenager's pallor, and an adult thinking it over: 'I mean...'
explanation.walkthrough: 'on reflection' reads A I MEAN backwards to give NAEMIA, after A from 'originally'.
explanation.definitionFit: Anaemia, a shortage of red blood cells, typically makes a sufferer look pale.

clue.text: Genuine extremists infiltrating reformed union is very clever

indicators.note: these letters get inside the other group, as spies infiltrate
reformed means made over again, so the letters of union is are rearranged
the extremes of a word are its outer letters, here of Genuine

explanation.surface: Real militants have cleverly infiltrated a reformed trade union.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reformed' makes INNIOUS from the union letters, and the genuine extremes go inside it after the first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone ingenious is inventive and resourceful, a synonym for very clever.

clue.text: Kind of fund for bad weather's aftermath

definitions.meaning: a reserve of money for bribes or illicit spending
the half-melted snow left after a storm

explanation.surface: A fund set aside to deal with the aftermath of a storm.
explanation.definitionFit: A slush fund is cash kept for shady purposes, and slush is the wet mess of melting snow.

clue.text: Remain undecided about old cleaner

indicators.note: the hovering word goes round the other letter

parts.note: to hover is to waver, unable to decide

explanation.surface: Someone dithers over buying an old cleaning machine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts HOVER round O.
explanation.definitionFit: Hoover is a brand of vacuum cleaner, long used in Britain as the general word for one.

clue.text: Porkies, soon heard regularly, getting an individual incarcerated

indicators.note: taking letters at a regular interval, the odd ones of these words

explanation.surface: Lies are soon heard at regular intervals when someone is locked up.
explanation.walkthrough: PORKIES is British rhyming slang (pork pies) for lies, which suits a prison story; 'regularly' takes the 1st, 3rd, 5th... letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A prisoner is a person held in jail, a synonym for someone incarcerated.

clue.text: One petitioning overthrow is keeping in charge

indicators.note: the first word holds the second inside it

parts.note: to supplant is to oust or overthrow a ruler

explanation.surface: A rebel's plea: overthrow the government but keep someone in charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is keeping' reads as part of the surface sentence; 'is' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A supplicant is someone who humbly begs or prays for something, a petitioner.

clue.text: Information on each record, it indicates variable pedigree

parts.note: gen is British slang for information
a log is a written record
y is a standard algebraic variable

explanation.surface: Data on each record suggests a family tree that varies.
explanation.walkthrough: GEN is informal British for information; in algebra x and y are the usual unknowns.
explanation.definitionFit: Genealogy is the study or account of a family's ancestry, its line of descent or pedigree.

clue.text: Similar things, essentially skilful abilities, lacking in you

indicators.note: the central letters go inside the old pronoun

parts.note: thee is the old form of you

indicators.note: the essence of each word is its central letter

explanation.surface: A put-down: you lack skilful abilities like those.
explanation.walkthrough: 'essentially' takes the middle letters of skilful, abilities and lacking, L I K, which go inside THEE. 'lacking' looks like a link but is one of the three words.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase 'and the like' means and similar things, other items of that kind.

clue.text: Time left to take in new marine storage facility

indicators.note: the two letters wrap round the rest, taking it in
something new is remade, so the letters of marine are reordered

explanation.surface: There's time left to build a new marine storage depot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges the marine letters into ERMINA, and 'to take in' has the time and left letters wrap round them.
explanation.definitionFit: A terminal can be a depot where oil or cargo is stored and distributed, as at a port.

clue.text: One short of the usual number of members, unfortunately?

definitions.text: One short of the usual number of members, unfortunately?

parts.words: One short of the usual number of members, unfortunately
parts.note: reads like a club or committee lacking a member, but members are limbs

explanation.surface: A club regrets being one member below its full complement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'members' suggests a club's membership; here it means arms and legs.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who has lost a limb has fewer limbs than normal, and members is an old word for limbs.

clue.text: Stirrer of trouble gutlessly a court supports

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting pieces sit beneath, so come after
without its guts, the inside letters, only the outer ones of trouble stay

parts.note: to spoon is an old word for courting or canoodling

explanation.surface: A cowardly troublemaker is backed by a court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gutlessly' leaves TE from trouble; A SPOON goes under it in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A teaspoon is the small spoon used to stir tea, a stirrer; the surface's stirrer of trouble is misleading.

clue.text: Gave up office, calmly accepting situation

definitions.meaning: having accepted something unwelcome without protest

explanation.surface: Someone quit their job and took it with equanimity.
explanation.definitionFit: To resign is to quit a post, and to be resigned to something is to accept it patiently.

clue.text: Join Central Essex Police? Nothing to lose

indicators.note: the central letter of Essex is its third
the letter for nothing is lost from the pieces

parts.note: O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: An invitation to join the local police force with nothing to lose.
explanation.walkthrough: ESSEX is an English county, and 'Central Essex Police' sounds like a real force. 'Central' gives S; 'to lose' takes O out of S + POLICE.
explanation.definitionFit: To splice ropes or film is to join two ends together.

clue.text: Irish city's being defaced continually

indicators.note: losing its face, the first letter is taken away

parts.note: Galway is a city on Ireland's west coast, with the possessive s

explanation.surface: An Irish city is constantly being vandalised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being defaced' removes G from the front of GALWAYS.
explanation.definitionFit: Always means at all times, without stopping, a synonym for continually.

clue.text: Is backing leading snooker player, having supportive position

indicators.note: going backwards, so the word is reads in reverse

parts.note: Ding Junhui, the top Chinese snooker professional

explanation.surface: A top snooker player is backed into a supportive position.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns IS into SI; Ding Junhui is a famous player from China.
explanation.definitionFit: Siding with someone means taking their part, a stance of support.

clue.text: Fight expected to be given approval ultimately

parts.note: due means expected, as a train due at noon

indicators.note: the ultimate letter of approval is its last

explanation.surface: A fight that's expected to win approval in the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A duel is a formal combat between two people, so a fight.

clue.text: Reject shop daughter enters was unoccupied

indicators.note: the letter goes into the reversed shop word
rejecting throws something back, so the shop word is read backwards

parts.note: a deli is a delicatessen shop

explanation.surface: A daughter wanders into a shop selling rejects, at a loose end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reject' turns DELI into ILED; 'enters' puts D inside after I.
explanation.definitionFit: To have idled is to have done nothing and had nothing to occupy one.

clue.text: Starts to disembark arriving into station platform

indicators.note: the starts of these words are their first letters

explanation.surface: A traveller gets off the train arriving at the station platform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Starts to' takes the first letters of four words.
explanation.definitionFit: A dais is a raised platform for speakers or a top table.

clue.text: Introduce stuff that can kick-start career

parts.note: to launch a product is to introduce it
to pad is to stuff with filling

explanation.surface: Promoting your stuff can kick-start your career.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that can kick-start career' defines a noun: something that gives a career a flying start.
explanation.definitionFit: A launchpad is where rockets lift off, and figuratively a springboard for success.

clue.text: Bending regularly at first stops being in pain

indicators.note: the letter plugs the word as a stopper does

parts.note: aching means feeling pain

indicators.note: the first letter of regularly

explanation.surface: Bending regularly at the start stops the pain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at first' gives R and 'stops' puts it inside ACHING after A.
explanation.definitionFit: Arching means curving the body or a structure into a bow shape, a kind of bending.

clue.text: Type of green American car

definitions.meaning: a bright green cloth, worn by Robin Hood's men
a luxury car made by Ford

explanation.surface: A green American car.
explanation.definitionFit: Lincoln green is a traditional shade named after the English city, and Lincoln is an American car marque.
